title: Switch fallthrough and scoping
recap: When a case has no break, execution continues into the next case. Fallthrough can be intentional, and the [[fallthrough]] attribute, or a fall-through comment, documents it so the compiler stays quiet.

Variables declared inside a case are visible to the whole switch, so a case that needs its own variable wraps its statements in a block. Stacked case labels share one set of statements without falling through.
objectives: Implement rankScore from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement rankScore. Valid ranks 0 through 3 start with 100 points. Rank 1 adds 10; rank 2 earns the rank-1 bonus plus 25; rank 3 earns both lower bonuses plus 50. Return -1 for invalid ranks. Practice a switch with intentional fallthrough and [[fallthrough]] between bonus cases; keep any case-local declarations in a block.
hints: Start with one score of 100 and add bonuses to it.
Begin at case 3 and fall through the lower ranks.
Reject invalid ranks before calculating bonuses.
